text:
Alice M: Heads up — after the kernel hotpatch last night we're seeing ~200 gpu_scrape_failure alerts in prod-us-west-2. DCGM exporter pods are Running but temp/power metrics are empty on a subset of nodes (gnode-3*, gnode-7*). Anyone seeing this? :warning:
DevInfraBot: Alert fired: gpu_scrape_failure (prod-us-west-2) — firing for 195 targets. See: https://prometheus.redwood.company/alerts/12345
Ben K: Which prometheus expr is firing? can you paste the query and a sample node id?
Alice M: The rule is basically `absent(dcgm_temp_celsius)` over node GPU targets. Sample node: gnode-3782-usw2. I can run `kubectl` if someone wants logs.
Rui T: I grabbed logs from the dcgm-exporter on that node:
```
kubectl -n infra logs ds/dcgm-exporter -l k8s-node=gnode-3782-usw2 --tail=200
... NVML: Failed to initialize: NVML_ERROR_UNKNOWN ...
```
Rui T: dmesg on that node shows a recent kernel message about `nvidia_uvm: module verification failed` right after the security hotpatch applied.
Carla S: hmm, so exporter up but NVML is failing under the new kernel. that would explain missing temp/power while other host metrics are fine.
Maya G: If NVML can't init, dcgm won't expose the device-level metrics. we should be careful about mass restarting kernel modules on prod. safe quick mitigation: mark the prometheus alert to require `dcgm_gpu_count > 0` and `container_ready==1` before firing, that would reduce noise while we triage.
Ben K: Suggest a short-term alert tweak: change the rule to `vector(1) unless (dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius or dcgm_gpu_power_watts)` is present AND `node_gpu_count > 0`. basically avoid alerting for nodes that have docker/driver issues. I can open a quick PR to alerts repo.
Alice M: I'm +1 for an alert tweak. can someone also try restarting the dcgm daemonset on the affected nodes as a test? prefer targeted restart rather than full roll.
Carla S: I'll cordon one affected node and do a targeted ds restart to verify behavior. stepping through: cordon -> drain (no eviction) -> kubectl delete pod -n infra -l k8s-node=gnode-3782-usw2 -> uncordon.
Rui T: After deleting the ds pod on gnode-3782-usw2 I see dcgm reinitialize and logs show `NVML initialized` then metrics appear. prometheus scrape for that target now returns temp/power again.
DevInfraBot: Alert resolved: gpu_scrape_failure (target gnode-3782-usw2) — resolved at 1812348900.
Ben K: OK rolling restarts on remaining affected nodes in small batches (3 at a time). I'll watch for driver-related kernel oops in syslogs. cc @Alice M for SLO impact.
Alice M: Good. initial rollout cleared ~60% of alerts. remaining ones are concentrated on two heterogeneous host pools that had a slightly older nvidia driver version.
Maya G: Follow-up actions we should track: 1) short-term: tweak alert rule to include `dcgm_gpu_count>0` and `container_ready` (PR opened by @BenK) 2) triage/update driver/kernel compatibility matrix (Carla to own) 3) add a Prometheus recording rule that marks nodes with 'nvml_initialization_failed' so alerts are less noisy 4) RFC to add an automated pre-patch check for NVML init on canary nodes before kernel patches roll out.
Carla S: I'll file the postmortem and start the driver/kernel compatibility doc. also recommend adding a tiny e2e that runs `dcgm-exporter --selfcheck` after node upgrades.
Ben K: PR merged to alerts (temporary tweak). also added a 30m silence window for the firing group until we confirm all restarts.
Rui T: Verified after rolling restarts + targeted driver updates on the two pools: metrics are stable and SLO dashboards show no tokenized GPU errors.
Alice M: Thanks all. I'll put this in the weekly all-hands notes under infra incidents and will open the RFC for pre-patch canary checks. :thumbsup:
Maya G: +1 on RFC. also worth adding a Grafana panel to show nvml_init_failures per node so we can triage faster next time.
Carla S: Postmortem link: https://wiki.redwood.company/infra/postmortems/dcgm-kernel-hotpatch-1812345678 (will fill in details).
